entries.test: Microsoft's canceled leases and abandoned expansion agreements would establish whether the forgone capacity exceeded one gigawatt.
entries.note: The capacity assertion is checkable; its alleged incompatibility with transformative AI is an interpretive conclusion.
The explanation attributes private doubts and motivations to Microsoft; cancellations alone cannot establish those beliefs.

entries.test: Microsoft's 2025 capital expenditure disclosures and hardware procurement reporting would show whether hardware upgrades accounted for anything close to $80 billion.
entries.note: The decisive assertion is the firm prediction that hardware upgrades would fall far short of the announced spending figure.

entries.test: SoftBank's investment commitments, available funds, asset sales and borrowing disclosures would establish the commitments and the financing gap described.
entries.note: The financial feasibility assertion has a plain balance-sheet reading despite 'does not appear.' The normalization selects the funding claim without the separate 55% calculation.

entries.test: OpenAI's reported cash resources, obligations and financing needs through March 3, 2026 would establish whether it needed additional money beyond the proposed $40 billion raise.
entries.note: The one-year deadline has passed. Raising additional money alone would not establish that it was necessary.

entries.test: Public financial reporting showing sustained OpenAI profitability or an unavoidable need for additional external funding would test the claimed lack of a path to profitability and consequent cash requirement.
entries.note: This is a categorical financial prediction without a deadline. Sustained profitability would provide a decisive counterexample.
The extracted adjectives are his own product judgments. 'Mediocre' supplies no agreed performance standard.
He reports his inability to see a survival route and his concern. He does not make a firm prediction that OpenAI will fail.
'This' encompasses the surrounding funding situation, not unambiguously just Son's remarks. The sentence assesses the available indications rather than firmly predicting Saudi funding.

entries.test: SoftBank's financing disclosures and OpenAI's cash-burn and model-serving cost reports would test whether the arrangement required continued borrowing and whether GPT-4.5 increased OpenAI's cash burn.
entries.note: The proposition combines a financial dependency claim with an undated prediction of increased cash burn caused by the new model.

entries.test: Published GPT-4.5 and GPT-4o prices, comparative evaluations and competing models' benchmark results would establish the price increase and performance differences.
entries.note: The surrounding text supplies concrete price and benchmark comparisons despite the evaluative adjectives.
This reports his own hesitation and its rationale. It does not announce that a bubble has burst.
He presents the pullback as suggesting a conclusion and raising doubts, rather than firmly asserting a particular growth outcome.

'Walking away from generative AI writ large' has no shared operational meaning, especially given his next sentence predicting continued sales. 'If I am correct' qualifies his interpretation rather than stating a future event condition.

entries.test: SoftBank's commitments, liquidity and borrowing disclosures through March 2026, together with public customer-level OpenAI revenue and cost evidence, would test the stated financing gap and universal customer losses.
entries.note: A demonstrated profitable OpenAI customer would refute the universal loss assertion. Company-wide losses do not establish losses on every customer.

entries.test: OpenAI's financing requirements and investor commitments, historical startup funding records and SoftBank's financing disclosures would test the claimed exclusive dependence on record funding financed by SoftBank debt.
entries.note: This asserts a present financing constraint. Evidence of sufficient alternative funding could refute the exclusivity claim.

entries.test: Public usage and retention studies, consumer adoption data outside ChatGPT, and research on AI coverage and its effects on adoption would test the claimed absence of mass-market uses and the proposed explanation.
entries.note: The passage makes an empirical adoption claim and explicitly attributes the alleged pattern mainly to coverage of OpenAI.
He urges readers to consider an interpretation of AI spending. This is not a firm prediction that generative AI will never grow.
